summary: Procurement and legal knock-through for Redwood onboarding at Crescent Health. Reviewed MSA/DPA open items, SLA appendix, pricing approval steps, and security documentation requirements. Agreed next steps: Redwood to send redlined MSA/DPA + SLA appendix; Crescent to confirm procurement timeline and security requirements. Technical onboarding scheduling planned after legal sign-off.

Private vs Dedicated deployment / VPC & KMS
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everybody, thanks for joining— appreciate you all making time. quick intro, I'm Maya, AE at Redwood. Liam is our SE, Priya on CSM.
[00:12] Sara Patel: Hi, Sara here from Crescent procurement. we have people from legal and security on. goal today is to get through the MSA and DPA open items and understand SLA/pricing path.
[00:25] Daniel Ruiz: yep, Daniel, counsel. main items for us are liability cap, indemnification, termination for convenience clause, and data processing obligations.
[00:35] Liam O'Connor: Great, we'll try to be succinct. quick note — we previously shared MSA v2 redlines, and there were three key asks from Crescent: increase liability cap, data deletion specifics, and SLA measurable metrics.
[00:50] Michael Lee: timeline wise, procurement needs sign-off by next Friday ideally. that will get budget release for Q1 pilot.
[01:05] Sara Patel: can you remind us what Redwood's standard liability cap is? i've seen both 1M and 5M in different versions.
[01:12] Maya Chen: Standard is $1M but we can discuss a $5M cap for enterprise contracts with a warranty carveout, and we have customers with tiered caps tied to committed spend. not a hard no, but will need approvals.
[01:27] Daniel Ruiz: okay we prefer higher; our legal prefers a cap at 3x fees and explicit carveouts for gross negligence — can you accept that?
[01:36] Maya Chen: we can explore a 3x fees approach, we normally push to include exceptions — we will flag for legal ops. i'll put that in the redline.
[01:45] Aisha Mohammed: From security side, we need SOC 2 Type II, current pen test report, and confirmation on customer key management — do you support KMS/HSM and BYOK?
[01:56] Liam O'Connor: yes — we support customer-managed keys via KMS integration, and HSM-backed options on private deployments. for hosted API we offer envelope encryption and key rotation; for Dedicated/Private we can do full BYOK. we'll attach our KMS integration guide.
[02:12] Jon Park: quick follow, our latency SLOs are strict for 100ms p50 and 500ms p95 for short prompt generation. do you have performance guarantees?
[02:24] Liam O'Connor: understood. Our SLA appendix can include throughput and latency targets for a named model and workload — usually we guarantee 99.9% uptime for hosted and an associated latency target for dedicated reservations. latency SLOs are trickier in hosted due to multi-tenant variability but with Dedicated we can commit to p95 numbers. i'll include measured benchmarks from similar customers.
[02:44] Sara Patel: and credits? what's the credit scheme if SLA missed?
[02:48] Maya Chen: we offer service credits by percentage of monthly bill depending on downtime window; we can propose a tiered credit schedule in the SLA appendix.
[02:56] Daniel Ruiz: on DPA, we need data residency assurances and deletion upon termination within X days plus a certificate of deletion. can you provide that?
[03:05] Liam O'Connor: yes — DPA supports data residency controls in certain regions, and for Private deployments data does not leave customer VPC. For hosted we can document retention, subset deletion flows, and provide attestation; we'll add a deletion SLA: e.g., 30 days to delete user data and provide an attestation.
[03:24] Aisha Mohammed: audit logs — we need 13 months of immutable logs and access to request logs for auditing. is that available?
[03:31] Priya Rao: we can provide audit log exports and retention tiers; longer retention is an add-on. We'll include the log retention options.
[03:38] Jon Park: on onboarding, what's the typical lead time for Dedicated or Private? we may prefer a Dedicated pool for predictability.
[03:45] Liam O'Connor: Dedicated provisioning is typically 4-6 weeks after contract and infra requisition. Private (VPC) can be 6-10 weeks depending on networking & approvals. Pilot on hosted API can start within a week for limited scopes.
[03:58] Michael Lee: procurement — we need the PO process and pricing cadence. what's the path for enterprise discounts?
[04:05] Maya Chen: discounts are tied to committed monthly spend and term length. we'll put a pricing sheet with committed tiers and projected unit costs. discounts and capex/opex treatment can be formalized in the commercial appendix.
[04:18] Sara Patel: any competitors' terms we should be aware of? i know some teams have pushed with PlatformX for lower cap, or Anthropic for SLOs.
[04:26] Daniel Ruiz: we habitually benchmark liability and data clauses.
[04:30] Liam O'Connor: noted. Redwood has some standard enterprise clauses we can share; i'll highlight where we can be flexible.
[04:36] [05:00] Speaker 1 (customer): there's a question about indemnification for third-party IP claims — do you carry that typically?
[05:06] Maya Chen: yes, we provide mutual indemnities for third-party IP infringement with standard carveouts. we avoid open-ended liability for customer data misuse.
[05:18] Daniel Ruiz: we also need to confirm export controls and regulated data handling — Crescent handles PHI in some workflows; does Redwood host any PHI in hosted?
[05:28] Liam O'Connor: Redwood does not ingest PHI unless under dedicated/private deployments with BAAs and scoped controls. for PHI workloads we recommend Private deployment or Dedicated with a BAA. i'll share our PHI handling policy and BAA template.
[05:44] Aisha Mohammed: encryption at rest and in transit — what's default?
[05:48] Liam O'Connor: TLS 1.2+ for transit, AES-256 at rest; BYOK/HSM available for private; customer can require FIPS-validated modules in contract.
[05:57] Sara Patel: can you point to the current SOC 2 report? we need the cert for our security review.
[06:02] Maya Chen: yes, link to SOC 2 Type II and pen test summary is in the shared drive — we'll include direct download links in the follow-up. (note: placeholder link: https://redwood.example.com/security/soc2-2026.pdf)
[06:18] Michael Lee: okay, commercial question — we have an internal approval process that requires CPL and a three-person sign-off. if we can land on 3x fees liability and SLA with credits, we can push to procurement.
[06:31] Daniel Ruiz: on termination, prefer 60 days notice for convenience and pro-rata refund for unused committed spend, not just future credits.
[06:40] Maya Chen: we typically do 30-90 day notice windows depending on term; pro-rata refunds for committed prepaid credits are something we can discuss — i'll flag that for legal.
[06:52] Jon Park: for integration, can you confirm available SDKs and webhooks? we need streaming responses and function-calling features.
[06:59] Liam O'Connor: SDKs in Python/Node/Go, streaming via websockets and structured function-calling available. we'll send integration guide and sample snippets.
[07:12] Sara Patel: procurement would like a single point cost estimate for a 6-month pilot and for a 12-month committed tier so we can compare.
[07:19] Maya Chen: we'll provide a pricing workbook with pilot and committed scenarios and ROI calc; i'll include token estimates for your expected usage patterns.
[07:28] [15:00] Priya Rao: quick recap of open items — MSA redlines (liability, termination, indemnity), DPA (deletion SLA and residency), SLA appendix (uptime, latency, credits), pricing workbook, SOC2 & pen test.
[15:18] Sara Patel: timeline: we target legal redline returned to Redwood by 12/10, Redwood responds 12/12, procurement sign-off 12/15 to get PO raised.
[15:28] Maya Chen: agreed, we'll aim to deliver redline and SLA appendix by 12/07 to accelerate.
[15:34] Daniel Ruiz: small thing — we insist on 3rd party subcontractor list for any subprocessors touching data.
[15:40] Liam O'Connor: we'll include the current subprocessors list and update commitments about notification windows for changes.
[15:48] Aisha Mohammed: one more, vulnerability disclosure policy and timeline for remediation for critical sev1 issues — can we get that?
[15:55] Priya Rao: yes, we'll include the vuln disclosure and typical remediation SLA in the security packet.
[16:03] Michael Lee: ok final question: onboarding resources and training — do you provide a dedicated CSM during pilot?
[16:10] Maya Chen: yes, Priya will be your CSM and will coordinate onboarding, runbooks, and weekly check-ins during the pilot.
[16:18] Jon Park: thanks — i'll wait for the tech docs.
[16:22] Sara Patel: thanks everyone. any other blockers?
[16:26] Maya Chen: none from our side. we'll follow up with the documents and redlines.
[16:33] Liam O'Connor: i'll attach benchmark CSV showing p50/p95 for a comparable health customer and the Dedicated commit options.
[16:42] Daniel Ruiz: we'll review and get back with legal redlines.
[16:48] Maya Chen: thanks all, we'll send the bundle and schedule follow-up for 12/09 to check progress.
[16:55] [END]
